title: Formation of the Philippine Archipelago

competencies.text: Demonstrate how the Philippine archipelago was formed.

days.title: Plate Tectonics
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will demonstrate how the Philippine archipelago was formed using plate tectonics, maps and cross-sections.

🌏 Earth's Layers

Earth has a thin rocky crust, a thick hot mantle, and a metallic core. The crust plus the rigid top of the mantle form the lithosphere, which is broken into large pieces called tectonic plates. They ride on the hotter, slowly flowing asthenosphere below.

🚚 Why Plates Move

Heat from Earth's interior drives slow convection currents in the mantle, and dense oceanic plates sinking at trenches pull the rest of the plate along. Plates move a few centimeters per year — about as fast as fingernails grow. Over millions of years, this adds up to hundreds of kilometers.

🧩 Three Kinds of Plate Boundaries

BoundaryMotionFeatures
ConvergentPlates move toward each other; one may sink (subduct)Trenches, volcanoes, strong earthquakes, mountains
DivergentPlates move apartRift valleys, mid-ocean ridges, new crust
TransformPlates slide past each otherEarthquakes along large faults; few volcanoes

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

choices.label: A large, rigid slab of lithosphere
A layer of liquid iron in the core
A cloud of hot gas in the mantle
A thin sheet of ice under the oceans

scenario.explanation: The lithosphere (crust plus upper mantle) is broken into large, rigid plates that move slowly.

scenario.text: What mainly drives the movement of tectonic plates?

choices.label: Mantle heat currents and sinking slabs
Ocean waves pushing against the coastlines
Strong winds blowing across the continents
The Moon's gravity pulling on the mountains

scenario.explanation: Mantle convection and the pull of sinking oceanic slabs move the plates.

scenario.text: At which type of boundary do plates slide past each other sideways?

choices.label: Transform
Convergent
Divergent
Subduction

scenario.explanation: At transform boundaries plates move horizontally past each other, causing earthquakes along faults.

days.title: The Plates Around the Philippines
days.content:
🗺️ A Country Between Plates

The Philippines lies in the Philippine Mobile Belt, a zone squeezed between the Philippine Sea Plate to the east and the Eurasian (Sunda) Plate to the west.

FeatureWhat happens there
Philippine Trench (east)The Philippine Sea Plate subducts westward under the archipelago; up to about 10,500 m deep
Manila Trench (west)Part of the Eurasian/Sunda Plate (South China Sea) subducts eastward under Luzon
Philippine Fault ZoneA long strike-slip (transform-type) fault, about 1,200 km from Luzon to Mindanao
Volcanic arcsChains of volcanoes above subducting plates: Mayon, Taal, Pinatubo, Kanlaon, Apo

✂️ Cross-Section of Subduction

Picture a slice through the crust: a dense oceanic plate bends and sinks into the mantle at a trench. As it descends and heats up, water released from it helps melt the mantle above. The magma rises and builds a line of volcanoes parallel to the trench. Friction between plates causes earthquakes.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each term to its description. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Theory that Earth's lithosphere is made of moving plates
match.why: It explains volcanoes, earthquakes and mountains.

match.right: Plates move together; one may subduct
Plates move apart and new crust forms
A denser plate sinks beneath another
match.why: It feeds volcanic arcs with magma.

match.right: Deep trench east of the archipelago
match.why: The Philippine Sea Plate sinks here.

match.right: Long strike-slip fault from Luzon to Mindanao
Belt of volcanoes and earthquakes around the Pacific
match.why: The Philippines is part of it.

days.title: How the Islands Formed
days.content:
🏝️ Building an Archipelago

The Philippines was not formed in one event. Over roughly the last 50 million years, several processes combined:

  1. Volcanic island arcs: subduction produced chains of volcanoes that rose from the sea floor and became islands.
  2. Uplift of ocean crust and sea-floor sediments: collisions pushed rocks once under the sea up into mountains. That is why marine fossils and limestone are found high on Philippine mountains.
  3. Drifting continental fragments: parts of Palawan and Mindoro are pieces of continental crust that broke from mainland Asia and drifted south-east before colliding with the island arc.
  4. Coral reef growth on the edges of islands built up limestone that was later raised.

🌊 Changing Sea Levels

During ice ages, sea level was much lower, and some islands were connected by land bridges. When sea levels rose, they became separate islands again — which helps explain why different island groups have different plants and animals.

🧭 Evidence Scientists Use

Rock types and ages, fossils, the location of volcanoes and earthquakes, magnetic records in rocks, and GPS measurements of plate motion today.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Use evidence to explain landforms. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: Geologists find fossil seashells near the top of a mountain in Mindanao. What is the BEST explanation?

choices.label: Plate collisions uplifted old sea floor
Birds carried the shells up from the beach
A tsunami washed the shells to the top
People threw the shells there long ago

scenario.explanation: Plate movements raised rocks that formed under the sea into mountains, carrying the fossils with them.

scenario.text: Mayon Volcano has erupted many times in recorded history. Why is it so active?

choices.label: It lies above a subduction zone that produces magma
It sits on a divergent ridge in the middle of Luzon
It is the tallest mountain in the whole country
Its slopes collect rainwater that turns into lava

scenario.explanation: Mayon is part of a volcanic arc formed above a subducting plate, where magma is continually generated.

scenario.text: Why is the Philippines made of thousands of islands instead of one large landmass?

choices.label: Arcs, uplift and drifting fragments built separate pieces
One large continent cracked apart during a single huge earthquake
Erosion by rain cut a single island into thousands of pieces
Rising sea levels covered a single flat plain all at once

scenario.explanation: Many separate geological processes over millions of years built islands in different places at different times.

scenario.text: Palawan's rocks are older and more like those of mainland Asia than the rocks of Luzon's volcanoes. What does this suggest?

choices.label: Palawan is a drifted piece of the Asian continent
Palawan formed from the youngest lava in the country
Palawan was built only by recent coral growth
Palawan sank and rose again in the last hundred years

scenario.explanation: Palawan's continental rocks show it broke away from the Asian mainland and later joined the archipelago.

scenario.text: A seismologist maps earthquakes and finds they get deeper going west from the Philippine Trench. What does this pattern show?

choices.label: A plate is sinking at an angle beneath the islands
The trench is filling up with sediment from rivers
The islands are moving east toward the Pacific
Earthquakes only happen near the ocean surface

scenario.explanation: Earthquakes along the sinking slab get deeper with distance from the trench, tracing the subducting plate.

days.title: Living on an Active Archipelago
days.content:
⚖️ Gifts and Dangers

BenefitsRisks
Fertile volcanic soils for farmingVolcanic eruptions (Pinatubo 1991, Taal 2020)
Geothermal energy (Leyte, Negros, Albay)Strong earthquakes (1990 Luzon, 2013 Bohol)
Mineral deposits: gold, copper, nickelTsunamis from undersea earthquakes
Mountains and coasts that support biodiversity and tourismLandslides on steep, uplifted slopes

📍 Know Your Place

PHIVOLCS publishes hazard maps showing active faults, volcanoes and tsunami-prone areas. The HazardHunterPH and GeoRiskPH platforms let anyone check the hazards at a specific location. Families, schools and LGUs use this information to choose safe building sites and plan evacuation routes.

🧠 Big Idea

The same plate movements that built our islands continue today. Understanding how the archipelago formed helps us live safely with its hazards and use its resources wisely.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: What theory explains that Earth's outer shell is broken into moving plates?

choices.label: Plate tectonics
Cell theory
Big Bang theory
Germ theory

escape.explanation: Plate tectonics describes the movement and interaction of lithospheric plates.

escape.text: At which type of boundary do volcanoes MOST commonly form above a sinking plate?

choices.label: Convergent
Transform
Divergent
Passive margin zone

escape.explanation: Subduction at convergent boundaries generates magma that rises to form volcanic arcs.

escape.text: The Philippine Fault Zone is mainly what kind of fault?

choices.label: Strike-slip fault
Divergent ridge
Subduction trench zone
Volcanic crater

escape.explanation: Blocks along the Philippine Fault move horizontally past each other — strike-slip motion.

escape.text: What is the Pacific Ring of Fire?

choices.label: A volcano and earthquake belt around the Pacific
A circle of coral reefs all around the equator line
A ring of hot ocean currents near Hawaii
A chain of deserts surrounding Australia

escape.explanation: The Ring of Fire follows subduction zones around the Pacific; the Philippines lies along it.

escape.text: Which Philippine agency monitors volcanoes and earthquakes?

choices.label: PHIVOLCS
PAGASA
DENR-EMB
NDRRMC

escape.explanation: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) monitors volcanoes, earthquakes and tsunamis.

escape.text: Which benefit comes from the same processes that form our volcanoes?

choices.label: Geothermal energy
Glaciers for water
Deserts for solar
Oil from coral

escape.explanation: Heat from magma beneath volcanic areas produces geothermal energy used in Leyte, Negros and Albay.
